title: 800 → 1000: Mastering Core Arithmetic & Reading Comprehension
focusAreas: Fractions, decimals, percentages, and basic linear algebra
Subject-verb agreement and fundamental sentence punctuation
Passage skimming vs active close reading
typicalWeaknesses: Gaps in pre-algebra foundations, reading fatigue, running out of time on module 1.
plateauBreakthrough: Focus purely on getting every Easy and Medium question correct. Skip difficult questions initially and ensure no points are lost on basic math operations.

title: 1000 → 1200: Solidifying High-Yield Grammar & Linear Equations
focusAreas: Standard English Conventions (comma rules, apostrophes, semicolons)
Slope-intercept form (y = mx + b), systems of equations
Transitions and Rhetorical Synthesis in Reading & Writing
typicalWeaknesses: Careless signs in algebra, guessing on rhetorical synthesis, passive reading of literature passages.
plateauBreakthrough: Grammar rules on the SAT are 100% predictable and rule-based. Memorizing punctuation boundaries guarantees a 50-80 point jump in Reading & Writing.

title: 1200 → 1300: Unlocking Advanced Math & Inference Skills
focusAreas: Quadratics, polynomials, exponent rules, and functions
Logical inference questions and command of textual evidence
Two-way probability tables and basic statistics
typicalWeaknesses: Falling for distractors in command-of-evidence questions, struggling with wordy math problems.
plateauBreakthrough: Do not read the full passage over and over. Identify the exact claim being made and match the strict textual evidence without extrapolating.

title: 1300 → 1400: Achieving Consistent Module 2 Hard-Routing
focusAreas: Mastering Desmos graphing shortcuts to solve hard questions in seconds
Circle theorems, trigonometry, and complex nonlinear systems
Words in context: building collegiate-level academic vocabulary
typicalWeaknesses: Getting routed to the easier Module 2 due to 3-4 careless errors in Module 1, time pressure in Module 2.
plateauBreakthrough: To score 1350+, you MUST qualify for the harder Module 2. Treat Module 1 like a minefield: double-check the first 15 questions before moving forward.

title: 1400 → 1500: Eliminating Careless Errors & Pacing Mastery
focusAreas: Rigorous error journaling in the Mistake Book
Graph and data interpretation in Reading/Writing (Quantitative Evidence)
Timing buffer: finishing Module 1 with 8+ minutes for review
typicalWeaknesses: Misreading 'Which of the following is NOT true?' or solving for x when the question asked for 2x + 1.
plateauBreakthrough: At 1400+, you know the concepts. Your enemy is misreading questions. Underline what is being solved for before writing down any math.

title: 1500 → 1550: Conquering the Hardest 5% of Digital SAT Items
focusAreas: Obscure vocabulary in context with subtle secondary definitions
Tricky constant problems (e.g., 'for what value of a does the system have no real solutions?')
Maintaining sustained cognitive focus across 2.5 hours without mental lapse
typicalWeaknesses: Losing 1-2 questions on subjective-feeling reading inferences, subtle algebraic edge cases.
plateauBreakthrough: Every missed question must be categorized by root cause. If you miss a question, explain WHY the 3 wrong choices are 100% indisputably incorrect.

title: 1550 → 1600: The Zero-Mistake Standard
focusAreas: Perfection across both sections with zero unforced errors
3-Pass Test Taking Method: Pass 1 (instant solves), Pass 2 (tough items), Pass 3 (audit all answers)
Psychological composure and handling unexpected problem formulations
typicalWeaknesses: Second-guessing correct answers, rushing in the first 5 minutes of a module.
recommendedResources: Full timed test simulations with official Bluebook proctoring
plateauBreakthrough: Never change an answer unless you can point to a concrete mathematical or textual proof that your first intuition was flawed.
